title: Reading and writing numbers up to six digits
description: From digits to words and from words to digits. What people actually write is accepted: with or without "and", with or without the hyphen, with or without the thousands comma.

questions.text: Write in digits: thirty-four thousand two hundred.
hints: Thirty-four thousands, and then two hundred
questions.explanation: 34,200. The thousands come first: 34 thousands are 34,000, plus 200.
Thirty-four thousand two hundred. The hyphen and the word "and" are both accepted, because both are written in practice.

questions.text: Write in digits: one hundred and five thousand and six.
hints: Watch the zeros nobody says out loud
questions.explanation: 105,006. The ten thousands, hundreds and tens are not named, and a zero holds each of their places.
Seven thousand and fifteen. The teens have their own names: not "ten five".

hints: Nine hundred thousands, and then forty

questions.text: Write in digits: two hundred thousand five hundred and twenty.
hints: Two hundred thousands and five hundred and twenty

questions.text: Which is larger, eighty thousand and ninety or eighty thousand and nine? Write it in digits.
hints: Write both in digits before comparing
questions.explanation: Eighty thousand and ninety is 80,090 and eighty thousand and nine is 80,009, so the larger is 80,090. They sound alike; written down they do not.

questions.text: Write in digits the largest six-digit number that repeats no digit.
hints: Start with the highest digit and work down
questions.explanation: 987,654: the highest digits go in the places that are worth most.

questions.text: A town has 12,480 inhabitants. Write that figure in words.
hints: Twelve thousands, four hundred and eighty
questions.explanation: Twelve thousand four hundred and eighty inhabitants.
